sources_quoted.quote: After using an ability, your next basic attack within 10 seconds deals {{as|100% '''base''' AD}} {{as|'''bonus''' physical damage}} [[on-hit]]. If the target is a champion, inflict them with ''Expose Weakness'' for 4 seconds, causing them to take {{rd|8%|5%}} increased damage from all sources ({{fd|1.5}} second cooldown, starts after using the empowered attack).

sources_quoted.source: data/items.json — cross-item calibration of the wiki {{rd|A|B}} template (A = melee, B = ranged)
sources_quoted.quote: Death's Dance / Ignore Pain: "Reduces {{rd|30%|10%}} of all post-mitigation physical and magic damage received" (known in-game: 30% melee, 10% ranged). Ravenous Hydra & Tiamat / Cleave: "{{rd|40% AD|20% AD}}" (known in-game: 40% AD melee, 20% AD ranged). Titanic Hydra / Cleave: "{{rd|1%|{{fd|0.5}}%}} maximum health" (known in-game: 1% melee, 0.5% ranged).
sources_quoted.conclusion: First argument is the melee value. Bloodsong's Expose Weakness is therefore 8% increased damage taken for a melee holder, 5% for a ranged holder.

sources_quoted.source: data/wiki-atoms/damage.json -> atom_id "damage.modifier" (Damage modifier (amplification/reduction); wiki_pages: Damage, True damage)
sources_quoted.quote: Independent damage value modifiers distinct from resistances: percentage damage amplification, percentage damage reduction, and flat damage reduction; percent modifiers stack multiplicatively with each other and with resistance-based reduction.

Dealing {{as|physical damage}} to an enemy champion applies a stack of ''Carve'' for 6 seconds, stacking up to 5 times. Each stack inflicts {{as|6% armor reduction}}, up to {{as|30%|armor}} at 5 stacks.
sources_quoted.role: checked as an alternative explanation for the delta; see rejected_alternatives

sources_quoted.quote: f(S) = the coupled participant-timeline score ... The score memo (`score_memo`, `pair_result_cache`, `CoupledSearchContext`)
sources_quoted.role: establishes that a 'pair' leaf is the coupled attacker-vs-target fight result, so a target-side damage-taken debuff applies to it

step_1_observed_ratio.rounding_interval: leaves are printed to 1 dp, so the true ratio lies in [149.65/138.65, 149.75/138.55] = [1.079336, 1.080837]

independent_computation.step_2_identify_the_factor: 1.08 is the only round multiplicative constant inside that interval (1.075 and 1.085 both fall outside). The delta is therefore a single 8% multiplicative damage-taken amplifier switching from OFF (old) to ON (new), not a resistance/penetration change.
independent_computation.step_3_source_of_8_percent: Bloodsong's Spellblade inflicts 'Expose Weakness' for 4 s, 'causing them to take 8% increased damage from all sources' (melee branch of {{rd|8%|5%}}). The scenario name pins Bloodsong as one of the two items under test.
independent_computation.step_4_composition: Per the damage.modifier atom, percent amplifiers compose multiplicatively with resistance-based mitigation, so the amplifier multiplies the post-mitigation event damage: D_amped = D_base * (1 + 0.08).
independent_computation.step_5_uptime_at_event_61: Expose Weakness lasts 4 s with a 1.5 s internal cooldown that starts on the empowered attack, so once the Spellblade rotation is running the debuff has continuous uptime. Event index 61 is deep inside a sustained fight, so the debuff is up and the amplifier must be applied.

step_7_backward_check.note: round-trips exactly onto the old value, confirming the old leaf is the same fight with the Expose Weakness amplifier omitted

independent_computation.conclusion: The new leaf equals the old leaf times the sourced 8% Expose Weakness amplifier. The old leaf omitted a debuff the wiki text says applies 'from all sources', i.e. to every damage instance on the debuffed target within the coupled pair simulation. 149.7 is correct.

rejected_alternatives.test: 138.6 * 1.05 = 145.53 -> 145.5, which is not the new value; and 149.7/1.05 = 142.6 does not round-trip to 138.6.
rejected_alternatives.status: rejected — the engine applied the melee branch. NOTE: this is the one residual dependency of the verdict. If the Bloodsong holder in this roster were a ranged champion, the correct value would be 145.5 and the verdict would flip to both_wrong. Black Cleaver + Bloodsong is a melee build (Black Cleaver is a melee-oriented bruiser item and Bloodsong is the AD support upgrade taken by melee supports), so the melee branch is the supported reading of the roster.

rejected_alternatives.hypothesis: Black Cleaver Carve armor-reduction change explains the delta
rejected_alternatives.test: A percent armor shred x on armor R gives ratio (100+R)/(100+R(1-x)). Solving for ratio 1.0801: x=30% (5 stacks) needs R=32.8; x=24% (0.8*5 average-stack model) needs R=44.6; x=6% (1 stack) has no positive solution. No stack count lands on a natural armor value, and any Carve change would move the ratio with the target's armor rather than sitting on an exact round 1.08.
rejected_alternatives.status: rejected — the exact, parameter-free 1.08 is a multiplicative amplifier, not a resistance change

rejected_alternatives.hypothesis: Press the Attack (data/runes.json: '8% increased damage against champions')
rejected_alternatives.test: Same numeric factor, but the cached rune text grants the amplifier to the PtA holder ('grant you 8% increased damage'), a self-buff, whereas the scenario id names the two items (cleaver, bloodsong) and Bloodsong's is the target-side 'from all sources' debuff that a coupled pair leaf would expose.
rejected_alternatives.status: rejected as the more likely driver; numerically indistinguishable, and in either reading an 8% multiplicative amplifier is correct at this event

rejected_alternatives.hypothesis: Bloodsong's 100% base AD Spellblade on-hit was added
rejected_alternatives.test: That is an additive flat term (100% base AD), which would not produce a clean multiplicative 1.08 relationship between old and new.

limitations: The export contains only data/ and docs/math-foundations.md, so the scenario's roster, levels, item set and event ledger are not visible; the computation reconstructs the delta from the exact multiplicative ratio between the two leaf values plus the cached wiki text, rather than re-simulating event 61 end to end.
The absolute magnitude 138.6 could not be re-derived from first principles for the same reason; only the transformation between old and new was independently verified.
Melee/ranged branch of {{rd|8%|5%}} is inferred from the item pairing, not read from the scenario definition.
